answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in autonomous agent networks, nodes must submit cryptographic proofs anchored to tamper-resistant hardware enclaves. A sable security module evaluates non-reproducible magnetic signatures from a ferrous core substrate, while a decentralized trust algorithm applies a ridge penalty to damp artificial reputation clusters. An attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities must incur massive physical capital expenditures to manufacture compliant hardware, making identity replication economically unviable.
